homepage.title: Different goals. Same need for proof.
homepage.lede: Everyone approaches cards differently. FlipForge gives them a disciplined way to understand their decisions.

framework.name: Get the decision, and the why

homepage.disclosure: Illustrative descriptions of how one FlipForge framework applies to different goals. FlipForge is decision support: it does not guarantee profit, investment returns or a grade, and it never buys or sells on your behalf.
homepage.closing: Different strategies. Different priorities. One standard for making an informed decision.

audiences.name: Collectors
audiences.pain: You want the card, but you do not want enthusiasm to hide weak evidence.
audiences.value: FlipForge separates the exact-card facts from the story and shows what still needs verification.
audiences.cta: Inspect the decision before you buy.

homepage.label: Collectors
homepage.headline: Love the card. Understand the purchase.
homepage.question: Is this the right card, and does the asking price make sense?

signals.identity: Year, set, number, parallel and grade are checked, so a similar-looking parallel is never mistaken for yours.
signals.evidence: You see which prices are reported sales of this exact card, at this grade, and which are asking prices or a different card.
signals.maxbuy: A supported value from qualifying sales shows whether the asking price is ahead of the evidence.
signals.decision: WATCH when the price runs ahead of the evidence. VERIFY when the card or its comparisons are unresolved.

homepage.why: You may never sell it. You still deserve to know it is the right card at a price the evidence supports.

audiences.name: Investors
audiences.pain: A chart can show what happened without telling you whether today’s opportunity is defensible.
audiences.value: FlipForge connects identity, evidence, economics, risk, and outcome tracking into one decision record.
audiences.cta: See the reasoning, not just the trend.

homepage.label: Investors
homepage.headline: Understand what supports the opportunity.
homepage.question: Does the available evidence justify committing capital?

signals.identity: The exact card is locked, so every later review looks at the same card.
signals.evidence: Evidence quality first: which sales qualify, how many there are, and how thin the market is.
signals.maxbuy: A supported value built only from qualified sales, and Max Buy at your own costs.
signals.decision: Risk and uncertainty stay visible. Saved decisions are frozen and can be reviewed at Days 7, 14 and 30.

homepage.why: Committing capital starts with what the evidence supports today and a record of why you acted. FlipForge does not forecast appreciation or returns.

audiences.name: Flippers
audiences.pain: An apparent spread disappears fast when comps are wrong, liquidity is weak, or costs are ignored.
audiences.value: FlipForge pressure-tests the spread before you commit capital.
audiences.cta: Test the margin before you chase it.

homepage.label: Flippers
homepage.headline: Find the margin before the mistake.
homepage.question: Is this actually a profitable opportunity after the costs and uncertainty?

signals.identity: Exact parallel and grade, so the spread is measured against the card you would actually resell.
signals.evidence: Only qualified sales count. Asking prices and stale sales are set aside, and a thin market is flagged as liquidity risk.
signals.maxbuy: Max Buy after your selling fees, shipping and target margin, and the cushion between it and the asking price. A break-even price for cards you own.
signals.decision: PASS when the margin is not there. WATCH when the cushion is thin.

homepage.why: A spread only exists after costs, and only while buyers are still there. FlipForge shows both before you commit capital.

audiences.name: Dealers
audiences.pain: Inventory decisions compound quickly when a weak comp or identity mismatch slips through.
audiences.value: FlipForge creates a repeatable decision process your inventory review can trace later.
audiences.cta: Make inventory decisions you can explain.

homepage.label: Dealers
homepage.headline: Make every inventory decision count.
homepage.question: Can this purchase be justified consistently and reviewed later?

signals.identity: Every card is checked against its exact identity, so a mismatched parallel does not enter inventory at the wrong cost.
signals.evidence: The same evidence rules on every card, with a reason for every price set aside.
signals.maxbuy: Pricing discipline: Max Buy at your own fees and margin, and a break-even price for each card you hold.
signals.decision: Each saved decision keeps its evidence and reasoning, so it can be traced and reviewed later.

homepage.why: When you buy many cards, consistency matters. The same rules on every card make each purchase explainable. You decide and you buy; dealer-specific workflows are not offered yet.

audiences.name: Grading users
audiences.pain: Population and grade spread matter, but they do not answer the whole purchase decision.
audiences.value: FlipForge keeps grading intelligence in context with evidence, economics, and uncertainty.
audiences.cta: Use grade context without losing the full decision.

homepage.label: Grading-focused buyers
homepage.headline: Look beyond the label.
homepage.question: Does the potential grade premium justify the purchase and associated risk?

signals.identity: Grader and grade are part of the card’s identity. A different grade is a different card.
signals.evidence: Grade-specific evidence: sales that name a different grader or grade, or that are marked raw, are set aside, so a price difference between grades is shown only where each grade has its own sales.
signals.maxbuy: Grading costs and possible outcomes are part of the economics, so a premium is tested against what it costs to reach it.
signals.decision: Grading uncertainty stays visible. VERIFY when the grader or grade cannot be confirmed.

homepage.why: A grade premium is real only when sales at that exact grade support it. FlipForge does not predict the grade a raw card will receive or guarantee a grading profit.
